findings.consequent: Information about object shape, background surface shape, and spatial arrangement
findings.quote: When an object casts its shadow on a background surface, the shadow can be informative about the shape of the object, the shape of the background surface and the spatial arrangement of the object relative to the background.

findings.consequent: Perception of spatial arrangement (depth)
findings.quote: Among all these roles, we found that cast shadows were perceptually most relevant for the recovery of spatial arrangement, especially when the shadow is in motion.

findings.consequent: Perception of surface shape
findings.quote: the human visual system does not effectively use cast shadows as cues to surface shape, despite the potential reliability of the information they provide.

findings.consequent: Perception of object motion in depth
findings.quote: moving cast shadows can produce a very vivid impression of an object moving in depth.

findings.antecedent: Manipulation of an object's cast shadow motion
findings.consequent: Perceived trajectory of the object
findings.quote: simply manipulating the motion of an object's cast shadow can dramatically change the perceived trajectory of the object.

findings.consequent: Perceived depth relations between surfaces
findings.quote: The effects of static cast shadows on perceived depth relations between surfaces is phenomenologically clear, as shown in Fig. 3. Their perceptual salience has also been demonstrated experimentally, particularly in their ability to anchor surfaces in depth when they are placed in a perspective rendering.

findings.antecedent: Moving only the cast shadow of a static object
findings.consequent: Percept of object motion in depth
findings.quote: By moving only the cast shadow of a static object in a scene, we were able to induce a strong percept of object motion in depth (despite the fact that the object did not move or change size in the image).

findings.consequent: Perception of square moving in depth
findings.quote: The proportion of times the square is perceived moving in depth increases when a penumbra is surrounding the shadow boundary, when the shadow displacement is consistent with a light located above the scene, and when the shadow is dark rather than light.

findings.antecedent: Shadow displacement consistent with light above scene
findings.consequent: Perception of square moving in depth
findings.quote: The proportion of times the square is perceived moving in depth increases when a penumbra is surrounding the shadow boundary, when the shadow displacement is consistent with a light located above the scene, and when the shadow is dark rather than light.

findings.antecedent: Shadow is dark rather than light
findings.consequent: Perception of square moving in depth
findings.quote: The proportion of times the square is perceived moving in depth increases when a penumbra is surrounding the shadow boundary, when the shadow displacement is consistent with a light located above the scene, and when the shadow is dark rather than light.

findings.antecedent: Changing contrast, opacity, or shape of shadow
findings.consequent: Perceived trajectory of the ball in space
findings.quote: the perceived trajectory of the ball in space was not affected by changing the contrast, the opacity or even the shape of the shadow.

findings.antecedent: Image sequence obtained by moving light source (instead of object)
findings.consequent: Perception of object moving in depth
findings.quote: Observers perceived a square moving in depth in Fig. 3 even when the image sequence was obtained by moving the light source rather than the square.

findings.antecedent: Adding more evidence that light was moving (e.g., more objects)
findings.consequent: Perceived trajectory of the ball
findings.quote: Adding more evidence that the light was actually moving, such as adding more objects in the scene, did not affect the perceived trajectory of the ball.

findings.consequent: Perception of square moving in depth (rather than background motion)
findings.quote: our observers preferred to see the square moving in Fig. 3 rather than the background.

findings.consequent: Perception of self-motion
findings.quote: This ambiguity between observer and object motion was never experienced: none of the observers in our experiments ever reported a perception of self-motion.

findings.consequent: Overriding of generic viewpoint constraint
findings.quote: the shadow motion clearly overrides the generic viewpoint constraint.

findings.consequent: Overriding of constant size cue and rigidity constraint
findings.quote: the cast shadow cue can override the generic viewpoint constraint, the constant size cue as well as the rigidity constraint is a qualitative index of the strength of the cast shadow cue for dynamic spatial layout perception.

findings.consequent: Local information about spatial layout
findings.quote: cast shadows are non-commensurate with other depth cues because they provide global rather than local information about spatial layout.

findings.antecedent: Cast shadows and other depth cues (size change, binocular disparity, motion parallax)
findings.consequent: Interaction in depth perception
findings.quote: an interaction between cast shadows and other depth cues has been found experimentally, in particular the cues of size change, binocular disparity and motion parallax.

findings.consequent: Distinguishing shadows from sharp surface markings
findings.quote: the presence of penumbra may help distinguish shadows from sharp surface markings.

findings.antecedent: Relative motion of an object and its cast shadow (constrained to follow a line connecting object to light source)
findings.consequent: Proper shadow labeling
findings.quote: In dynamic scenes, a feature appears which can very reliably determine proper shadow labeling: the relative motion of an object and its cast shadow is constrained to follow a line connecting the object to the light source.

findings.consequent: Reliable cue to shadow labeling
findings.quote: The importance of correlated motion as a cue to shadow labeling may explain the divergent phenomenal effects of violating luminance constraints in the square-above-the-checkerboard movie and the ball-in-a-box movie.

findings.consequent: Reliable source of information for linking cast shadows and objects
findings.quote: In dynamic scenes, in which both objects and their cast shadows are moving, the correlated motion between an object and its shadow provides a reliable and simple source of information for linking cast shadows and objects.
